about: Africa's rare-earth projects at feasibility stage or beyond, with owners, stage, resource, buyers and lenders, each fact with the address it was read from. Compiled for the Africa Infra Watch minerals page (draft). Coordinates: the project's own report where published, otherwise the USGS deposit point of the same name (loc_precision 'usgs'), otherwise none. Mineral-sands mines that hold monazite count only where the operator reports recovering or selling it: QMM in Madagascar does; Kenmare's Moma, Richards Bay Minerals and Namakwa Sands disclose no rare-earth tonnage and are under left_out.

stages.producing: Producing, or commissioning with first product
stages.feasibility: Feasibility study done or under way, permits sought
stages.exploration: Resource defined or being defined, scoping study at most
stages.stalled: Suspended, licence revoked or in dispute

facts.text: Madagascar's USGS figure does not come from mine reports. It is "estimated based on reported import data for China".

USGS cut its estimate of Nigeria's 2024 output from 13,000 t REO (January 2025 edition, estimated from Chinese import data) to 1,500 t (February 2026 edition). Madagascar's 2024 figure fell from 2,000 t to 1,400 t.

Tanzania (890,000 t REO) and South Africa (860,000 t) are the only African countries with quantified rare-earth reserves in the USGS table. World reserves exceed 75 million t, and USGS records no mine output from either country in 2024 or 2025.

In June 2025 the EU named 13 'Strategic Projects' outside the bloc under its Critical Raw Materials Act. The only two rare-earth projects among them are African: Mkango's Songwe Hill in Malawi and Frontier Rare Earths' Zandkopsdrift in South Africa.

The US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) said in August 2026 that it had committed $62.8 million to rare-earth projects in Malawi, Angola, Madagascar and South Africa, none yet in production. Most of it is the $50 million it would put into TechMet's option on a stake in Phalaborwa, which Rainbow Rare Earths' own filings describe as not yet exercised.

Malawi banned exports of raw, unprocessed minerals from 21 October 2025 by presidential executive order. Rare earth elements are named in the order's list, but minerals processed in Malawi are exempt.

In June 2023 Namibia's Cabinet banned exports of unprocessed critical minerals, and rare-earth minerals are named in the ban. Small quantities can still be exported at the mines minister's discretion, with Cabinet endorsement.

The African Union's Green Minerals Strategy, adopted by the AU Executive Council in February 2025, says rare earths are mined in Angola, Burundi, Madagascar and South Africa. It lists projects in development in Malawi, South Africa, Tanzania, Madagascar, Morocco and Mozambique.
In April 2025 China tightened export controls on several rare earths, including terbium and dysprosium, and kept those controls after suspending a wider October 2025 extension.

export_rules.text: Cabinet banned exports of unprocessed critical minerals: crushed lithium ore, cobalt, manganese, graphite and rare-earth minerals. Smaller quantities may be exported at the mines minister's discretion, subject to Cabinet endorsement. The decision was announced by Deputy ICT Minister Emma Theofelus at a Cabinet briefing. No gazette notice was found.

A presidential executive order banned exports of raw, unprocessed minerals from 21 October 2025. It names uranium, rare earth elements, niobium, graphite, tantalum and others, and exempts minerals processed, refined or value-added in Malawi. Lindian Resources says Kangankunde is unaffected because it will export a concentrate.
In his February 2026 State of the Nation address, President Mutharika suspended all new mining licences and ordered an audit of existing permits. The October 2025 raw-export ban stays in place.

The 2017 overhaul of the Mining Act gives the government a non-dilutable free-carried interest of at least 16% and restricts exports of raw resources for beneficiation abroad. This applies to all minerals. At Ngualla, Tanzania holds a 16% free-carried interest in Mamba Minerals, the licence holder.
A ban on exporting unprocessed minerals, imposed by President Museveni in February 2015, 'still stands', Energy Minister Ruth Nankabirwa said in October 2022. Rare earths are not named.

No gazetted ban was found. Nigeria makes local processing a condition of new licences, and Solid Minerals Minister Dele Alake said in May 2025 that 'The days of exporting raw minerals from pit to port are over.' Rare earths are not named.

deals.text: The DFC made a $50 million equity investment in TechMet to support the Phalaborwa Rare Earths project in South Africa, which will reprocess gypsum waste from legacy mining. The project needs about $317 million in total.

deals.text: The EU-Namibia memorandum of understanding on sustainable raw materials and renewable hydrogen, signed at Sharm El-Sheikh (COP27), is non-binding. It cites rare earth elements for permanent magnets as an example of the critical raw materials it covers.

The EU named Songwe Hill (Malawi, Mkango Resources) and Zandkopsdrift (South Africa, Frontier Rare Earths) as Strategic Projects under its Critical Raw Materials Act. They are 2 of the 13 projects outside the EU, which need about EUR 5.5 billion in total capital.

usgs_mcs2026.reserves_note: USGS lists Madagascar and Nigeria reserves as NA (not available). It shows South Africa and Tanzania production as a dash, meaning zero. Units are metric tons of REO equivalent. No other African country has its own row; any other African output is inside 'Other' (1,000 t in 2024, 550 t in 2025). Reserves for ZA and TZ are the same in the 2025 and 2026 editions.
footnotes: [MCS 2026, header] Data in metric tons, rare-earth-oxide (REO) equivalent, unless otherwise specified
[MCS 2026, fn 1] Data include lanthanides and yttrium but exclude most scandium.

[MCS 2026, fn 12, attached to Madagascar 2024 and 2025 and to Burma, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam; NOT attached to Nigeria] Estimated based on reported import data for China. Source: Trade Data Monitor Inc.

[MCS 2026, World Mine Production and Reserves] Significant revisions were made to the 2024 production for Australia, Brazil, Burma, Madagascar, Nigeria, and Vietnam based on Government and industry reports.
[MCS 2025, fn 12, attached to Madagascar and Nigeria 2023 and 2024] Estimated based on reported import data for China. Source: Zen Innovations, Global Trade Tracker.

[MCS 2025, Events, Trends, and Issues] Global mine production was estimated to have increased to 390,000 tons of REO equivalent largely owing to increased mining and processing in China, Nigeria, and Thailand.

[MCS 2026, Yttrium chapter] Although mined rare earth production in Burma, India, Madagascar, Malaysia, Nigeria, and Thailand was significant, reliable information on yttrium reserves was not available.

madagascar_output.text: USGS MCS 2026 estimates Madagascar REE mine output at 2,700 t REO in 2025 (1,400 t in 2024). A footnote says both figures are estimated from reported Chinese import data (Trade Data Monitor), and no operation is named. USGS's 2019 Minerals Yearbook names QMM (Rio Tinto 80%/state 20% then, Mandena) as the country's REE producer, recovering monazite from tailings since 2018: about 4,000 t REO in 2019, with capacity around 4,400 t REO. Rio Tinto says QMM produces monazite, and The Ecologist (Feb 2026) reports QMM ships it to China. The 2025 figure is consistent with QMM monazite exports, but no fetched source attributes it explicitly. Vara Mada and Ampasindava are not producing.

nigeria_output.text: USGS MCS 2026 gives Nigeria 1,500 t REO mine production in both 2024 and 2025, reserves NA. That is a big cut from MCS 2025, which put Nigeria at 7,200 t (2023) and 13,000 t (2024), with a footnote saying the figures were estimated from Chinese import data. MCS 2026 says the 2024 Nigeria figure was significantly revised 'based on Government and industry reports'. The USGS 2024 Nigeria chapter (data to Mar 2026) tabulates monazite concentrate at 210 t (2020), 590 t (2021e), 2,535 t (2022), 2,620 t (2023) and 2,600 t (2024e). Its separate oxide-content row runs 110, 300, 1,300e, 1,400e and 1,400e t REO. Monazite concentrate is the only rare-earth mineral USGS tabulates for Nigeria. USGS says monazite mining restarted in 2017, and that critical minerals in Nigeria are produced by artisanal and small-scale miners as well as private companies. It names no monazite mine, area or buyer. It records tin ores and concentrates going to China. The federal research council RMRDC sampled monazite in Kano, Taraba, Plateau, Kaduna and Bauchi in 2025. A private Nigerian seller was offering 55-60% REO monazite concentrate in Aug 2026. No gazetted ban on raw-mineral exports found; the minister's Oct 2023 line that 'the era of exporting raw materials is over' is a policy statement. No Chinese-built REE plant found; the Chinese plant the USGS chapter names in Nasarawa processes lithium.

left_out.name: Glenover (Limpopo)
left_out.why: Owned by Afrimat (JSE) since 2021, not Fertoz. Only a techno-economic assessment / concept study has been done for rare earths (SAMREC 19.47 Mt @ 1.52% TREO+Y2O3; 647 ha mining right; phosphate stockpiles processed). Afrimat says it is still optimising the flowsheet. No PFS or DFS. Metallurgical test work was done in South Africa, China, Germany and the USA. Sources: https://www.afrimat.co.za/future-materials-metals/ and https://www.afrimat.co.za/press-releases/the-glenover-rare-earth-project/

open_questions: Phalaborwa DFC: Miningmx (5 Oct 2026) says DFC 'has already committed $50m towards construction funding'. Rainbow's Dec 2023 RNS and Mar 2026 interims call it a US$50m equity option via TechMet, not exercised. DFC's Apr 2024 public summary says DFC 'proposes to invest up to $50 million in equity' (https://www.dfc.gov/sites/default/files/media/documents/9000116135.pdf). Treat it as an option unless DFC or Rainbow confirm.
Phalaborwa: did Bosveld complete the notarial lease and the transfer of the stacks to an SPV (long-stop 31 Dec 2025)? Rainbow's option to buy Bosveld's 15% for 38.9m new shares runs to 30 Jun 2027.

Phalaborwa: Rainbow's website still says first production from 2028; Oct 2026 reporting says early 2029. The 1,800 tpa NdPr figure is from the Dec 2024 interim study and may change in the Q4 2026 PFS.

Phalaborwa foreign ties: TechMet (Irish-registered, DFC-backed) holds 10.7% of Rainbow (https://www.rainbowrareearths.com/investors/shareholder-information/major-shareholders/). Offtaker Neo (Toronto HQ) has plants in Canada, Estonia, China, Germany, Thailand and the UK. Traxys and two US family offices joined the Mar 2026 GBP 11.1m (c. US$14.6m) raise (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/rainbow-rare-earths-limited-npv--rbw/subscription-raises-11-1m-from-investors/9499206). Rainbow is registered in Guernsey (Mar 2026 interims: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/rainbow-rare-earths-limited-npv--rbw/interim-results-for-six-months-to-31-december-2025/9500041), hence home GG.

Steenkampskraal: the stake split between Steenkampskraal Holdings and Bora is undisclosed. SHL's country of incorporation was not found (no UK Companies House entry). Bora appears as both 'Bora Mining Services' (2024) and 'Bora Mining Investments' (company site). Bora's ZA home is taken from boramining.co.za (Midrand head office, '100% Black Owned').

Steenkampskraal: stage set to producing on the company's statement at the 6 Oct 2026 opening that 'Production is under way'. No shipment has been confirmed yet, so it could still be read as commissioning.

Steenkampskraal: the company overview says the mining right runs 20 years from 2 Jun 2010 (renewable), which matches the undated sentence on the licences page, so the 2030 expiry is probably the mining right's. COR-23 dates are unconfirmed. The reserve excludes a pending Section 102 extension. The NI 43-101 report date is not stated. The site's text says 665,000 t @ 14.5%, but its table gives 605,000 t @ 14.4%.
Steenkampskraal: the IDC funding amount and its terms (loan or equity) are undisclosed.

Zandkopsdrift: reserve tonnage and grade from the 2025 updated PFS were not found. Older figures such as 41.12 Mt @ 1.92% TREO (c. 2015) appeared only in search snippets and were not verified. Stakes of Frontier, IDC, KOMIR and the BEE holders are unknown. No coordinates were found in a fetched source.
Zandkopsdrift: Frontier says multiple EU funding pathways are being evaluated (News24, Feb 2026). Watch for EU, EIB or Carester-linked finance.

Malawi export rules: Presidential Executive Order No. 2 of 2025 bans raw-mineral exports; the MMRA letter of 28 Oct 2025 says Kangankunde is exempt because monazite is concentrated in Malawi before export. Draft Beneficiation and Value Addition Regulations and amendments to the Mines and Minerals Act 2023 were under consultation until 10 Oct 2026. https://wcsecure.weblink.com.au/clients/lindianresources/headline.aspx?headlineid=61346521 ; Mining Minister quoted 24 Sep 2026 saying no company may export raw minerals: https://www.nyasatimes.com/lindian-resources-moves-to-upgrade-licence-as-malawi-tightens-mineral-export-rules/

Kangankunde licence class: the Malawi parliament (4 Aug 2026) said the operation is large-scale but runs on a medium-scale licence; the Attorney General (14 Aug 2026) said Rift Valley Resource Developments applied to upgrade and MMRA was to meet the company on 19 Aug 2026. Outcome not found. https://allafrica.com/stories/202608040027.html ; https://justice.gov.mw/node/566

Kangankunde state stake: no fetched source states a Government of Malawi equity interest or a Mining Development Agreement. Mkango's disclosures say the government may take a free 10% on grant of a large-scale licence, so an upgrade might bring one in (inference, unconfirmed).

Kangankunde US interest: US Deputy Assistant Secretary of State Nicholas Checker visited in Dec 2025 to discuss a possible partnership; no US funding announced. https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-industry/1812-51499-us-interest-in-malawi-rare-earths-extends-to-kangankunde-project

Kangankunde downstream: Lindian owns the SARECO MREC plant in Stepnogorsk, Kazakhstan (formerly Kazatomprom), meant to process Kangankunde concentrate; Carester (France) has a binding 10-year offtake for 70% of SARECO heavy rare earth product, and a Gerald Metals sale agreement was terminated in Jun 2026. https://wcsecure.weblink.com.au/clients/lindianresources/headline.aspx?headlineid=61345643
Kangankunde licence date: April 2022 comes from a parliamentary report quoted by allAfrica; exact day not found.

Songwe tenure: the 2022 NI 43-101 report lists Retention Licence RTL 0001/21 granted 1 Jun 2021, valid to 1 Jun 2026 (non-extendable), and Mkango said in Sep 2026 that the large-scale mining licence is still not granted, so current tenure is unclear. https://minedocs.com/22/Songwe_Hill-TR-070121022.pdf

Songwe export: the Mar 2026 DFS lists Malawi government approval to sell the MREC as a risk; the MREC is to go to Mkango's planned Pulawy plant in Poland for separation. https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mkango-resources--mka/feasibility-study-songwe-pfs-results-pu-awy/9481471

Ngualla China link: Shenghe (Aug 2026) says the project awaits Chinese technology-export approval. Reuters reported in Sep 2026 that state-owned China Rare Earth Group is in talks to buy control of Shenghe; Shenghe denied it, citing its controlling shareholder, the Institute of Multipurpose Utilisation of Mineral Resources. https://www.businessday.co.za/world/international-companies/2026-09-20-how-shenghe-deal-could-reshape-us-and-australias-rare-earth-stakes/

Tanzania rules: law gives the state not less than 16% non-dilutable free-carried shares in a mining company and a right to acquire up to 50%. Peak and the government also set up Mamba Refinery Corp (84/16) and studied a Tanzanian refinery, with a longer-term plan for a mixed carbonate plant in Tanzania. https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20250811/pdf/06mrcb48sjb3qs.pdf

Teesside (UK): Peak secured a site for a rare earth refinery, then dropped it in favour of a standalone concentrate project and sold it on 9 Jul 2025 for GBP 3.5m. https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20250811/pdf/06mrcb48sjb3qs.pdf

Ngualla takeover price: shareholders were paid A$0.443 per share on 30 Sep 2025, above the A$0.359 minimum in the May 2025 deal (total A$157.99m at signing). Press reports of an A$195m final value were not verified.
Ngualla output: older press cites 37,200 t/y concentrate; the Aug 2025 scheme booklet gives 16.2 kt/y. The booklet figure is used.
Ngualla coordinates are from Wikipedia (Mount Ngualla), not a technical report; treat as approximate.

Wigu Hill: former owner Montero Mining agreed to settle its dispute with Tanzania over the project for US$27m in three instalments (date not visible on page). https://www.northernminer.com/news/montero-mining-settles-with-tanzania-for-us27m/1003875175/ No Vital Metals update on the licence after 2023 was found.

Songwe MDA: Mining Development Agreement signed 26 Jul 2024 (announced 29 Jul 2024) with a 5% royalty on gross revenue and a 10% non-diluting equity interest for the Malawi Government. https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/mkango-resources--mka/mkango-signs-mda-with-malawi-government-for-songwe/8334631

Ngualla licence changes: the SML area was expanded from 18 to 51 km2 and the initial term extended to 30 years (announced 26 Apr 2024). https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20250811/pdf/06mrcb48sjb3qs.pdf

Kangankunde licence detail: Lindian names it Mining Licence MML0290/22 (medium-scale) and says approval was given during FY2026 to enlarge the area from about 900 to 2,500 ha. https://wcsecure.weblink.com.au/clients/lindianresources/headline.aspx?headlineid=61345643

Namibia: Cabinet in June 2023 banned export of unprocessed critical minerals 'such as' crushed lithium ore, cobalt, manganese, graphite and rare earth minerals, with ministerial exemptions for small volumes (https://www.mining-technology.com/news/namibia-ban-unprocessed-minerals-export). Lofdal's DFS now aims to make separate light and heavy rare earth carbonates in Namibia, aligned with domestic beneficiation goals (https://www.namibiacriticalmetals.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/260720-NMI-Press-Release-Budget-SGS-FINAL-.pdf). Current enforcement status of the ban not checked.

Uganda: ban on export of unprocessed minerals in place since Feb 2015, restated by the energy minister in Oct 2022 (https://www.monitor.co.ug/uganda/news/national/ban-on-raw-minerals-export-to-stay-govt-3982402). Unclear whether Makuutu's mixed rare earth carbonate counts as processed.

Makuutu ownership: Ionic still reports 60% of Rwenzori Rare Metals (June 2026 quarterly, https://investorpa.com/announcement/322913/); the Dec 2023 conditional purchase of a further 34% from Rare Earth Elements Africa (to 94%) has not been shown as completed. Holders of the remaining stake not verified.

Makuutu state participation: in Feb 2023 Ionic said a mineral development agreement under negotiation gives the Ugandan government an option for a free carry or an interest up to 15% (https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/ionic-rare-earths-ixr-us-funders-want-to-secure-heavy-rare-earths); no current confirmation found.

Makuutu China/US links: Apr 2021 non-binding MoU with Chinalco subsidiary China Rare Metals and Rare Earth (Jiangsu) covering potential offtake and funding (https://www.mining-technology.com/news/ionicre-mou-makuutu-rare-earths-project/); by Jul 2026 Ionic says output is not committed to China and cites US partner talks. Makuutu was also added to Minerals Security Partnership discussions per https://ionicre.com/makuutu/.

Makuutu DFS numbers (about 1,300 tpa REO first 10 years, 172.9 Mt reserve @ 848 ppm, capex US$120.8m) were seen only in search snippets; the Mar 2023 ASX PDF could not be read, so they are not in the record.

Makuutu licence date: company table says LML00334 granted 28 Dec 2023; it was signed by the energy minister in Kampala on 17 Jan 2024 and was the first large-scale licence under the Mining Act 2022 (https://www.globalminingreview.com/exploration-development/19012024/ionic-rare-earths-project-mining-licence-signed-by-ugandan-government/).

Longonjo ownership: Angolan state 10% and other Angolan partners 6% come only from Ecofin (Mar 2026); Pensana's filings say only that minority shareholders are free-carried (https://pensana.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Pensana-integrated-annual-report-2025.pdf). FSDEA's own stake in Ozango after its US$25m (which cut Pensana from 84% to 68.4%) is not disclosed; the 10%/6% may predate that dilution.

Longonjo debt: AFC approved US$81.2m of the ~US$160m loan plus a US$54.9m convertible in Mar 2025, but 2026 updates describe only Absa debt backed by US EXIM (https://pensana.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Operational-Update-8th-June-2026.pdf). Is AFC still in? The debt had not closed by 25 Sep 2026.

Longonjo Gulf money: Cascade Natural Resources terms shifted. Apr 2026 said 38.2% of Sable Min for US$150m; the June 2026 update says about 4% of Pensana and of Sable Min; Aug 2026 says State of Qatar backers widened scope to downstream and a NASDAQ listing, with US$150m still outstanding (https://pensana.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Update-on-Cascade-Financing-6-August-2026.pdf). Appointment of Sheikh Dr Badr bin Dalhim Al-Faheid Al-Hajri to Cascade's board was not yet effective on 17 Aug 2026 (https://pensana.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Update-on-Strategic-Investor-Board-Appointment.pdf).

Longonjo schedule slip: first production 2027 (Mar and Jun 2026), then 2028 at about 25% complete (https://pensana.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/Trump-announces-US3-billion-support-for-U.S.-critical-minerals-supply-chains.pdf), then late 2028 (Sep 2026).

Pensana strategy: NASDAQ listing planned for mid-2026 (Dec 2025) not done by Sep 2026. Saltend (UK) separation design is being re-optimised for deployment in 'the most operationally and commercially advantageous location', alongside a US mine-to-magnet chain with eVAC in South Carolina and Japanese partners; Hanwa is sponsoring a separation study under Japan's METI Global South initiative (https://pensana.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Operational-Update-8th-June-2026.pdf).

Longonjo and the Lobito corridor: MREC to be railed 273 km to Lobito; Pensana cites the US DFC-backed US$553m rail concession financing and EU support (https://pensana.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Construction-on-track-for-2027-first-production.pdf).

Lofdal JOGMEC stake history (verified): 40% after Term 2 (C$10m) as of Jan 2026 (https://www.namibiacriticalmetals.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/130126-NMI-Press-Release-PFS-Filed-on-SEDAR-FINAL.pdf); Mar 2026 amendment raised Term 3 from C$10m to C$13m (total C$23m) (https://www.namibiacriticalmetals.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/260330-NMI-Press-Release-JV-Amendment-SEDAR.pdf); 50% earned Jul 2026 via TJNREC. NMI's 45% is implied by the release (NMI may participate up to 45%; HDN 5%); company boilerplate still prints NMI 95% / HDN 5% at subsidiary level.

Lofdal approvals: on 31 Aug 2026 NMI said shareholder consent, regulatory approvals and final TSX-V approval were still pending for the TJNREC transaction (https://www.webull.com/news/15499415444530176).

Lofdal DFS timing: company target Q2 2027 (Mar 2026 release) vs Q3 2027 in Crux Investor (Aug 2026, https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/namibia-critical-metals-secures-new-partner-and-funding-for-lofdal-heavy-rare-earth-project-towards-fid). PFS reserve 32 Mt @ 0.176% TREO, capex US$347.9m, after-tax NPV5 US$275.5m (https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/namibia-critical-metals-reports-positive-pre-feasibility-study-for-lofdal-heavy-rare-earths-project).
Lofdal ML 200 exact grant date: expiry 10 May 2046 implies grant around May 2021 (11 May 2021 per an unfetched 2024 technical-report snippet); announced 22 Jul 2021.
Coordinates: none found in a fetchable primary source for Makuutu or Lofdal (the Lofdal NI 43-101 PFS PDF is over 10 MB). Longonjo uses town coordinates as an approximation.
Madagascar 2025 output (USGS 2,700 t REO): no source names the operation. It is consistent with QMM monazite shipped to China, but this attribution is unconfirmed. See madagascar_output.

Ampasindava: no arbitration found. Fetched history shows a 2011-2023 national moratorium on new mining licences and ownership churn rather than arbitration: Tantalus/TRE AG bankrupt 2015, then REO Magnetic, ISR Capital/Reenova (SG), GRM (2021) and Harena (Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampasindava_mine). Confirm with Madagascar's mining cadastre (BCMM).

Ampasindava Chinese link: Reenova Investment Holding (SG, 75% holder at the time) signed a non-binding MOU with China Nonferrous Metal Industry's Foreign Engineering and Construction Co. (NFC, Shenzhen-listed) on 24 Jun 2019 (SGX filing https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/42Z73Y5GBREB57C4/574835_RIHL%20-%20Announcement%20-%20Quarterly%20Update%20Listing%20Rule%201313.2%20for%202Q2019%20-%2015%20Aug%202019.pdf). Not followed by any known deal.

Ampasindava: the exploitation permit number, grant date, term and area are not in the 12 Oct 2026 RNS. Licence PR6698 appears only in secondary coverage, which was not fetched. Some outlets give the DFC amount as $4.48m, but the RNS says $4.84m. Harena signed the Cahier des Charges Minières (CCM) on 11 Aug 2026 (RNS https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/harena-resources-plc--hree/mining-terms-and-conditions-ccm-signed/9714357). Reuters via Engineering News (https://www.engineeringnews.co.za/article/us-backs-madagascar-rare-earths-project-in-push-to-loosen-chinas-supply-chain-grip-2026-07-28, Jul 2026) named MP Materials, USA Rare Earth and Solvay (EU) as potential refining partners; no offtake is signed.

Vara Mada: no news on the investment agreement after Aug 2026. AllAfrica (May 2026) says it must be approved by the High Constitutional Court and Parliament before work starts (https://allafrica.com/stories/202605040006.html). No Madagascar state equity is disclosed; the Dec 2024 MOU reportedly includes a 5% royalty, but this was not fetched. Coordinates were not found.

QMM: the monazite resource/reserve was not fetched (Rio Tinto 20-F too large). Monazite volumes since 2019 and buyer names are undisclosed. The Ecologist reports operations were suspended Nov 2025 to 6 Jan 2026, which may explain a lower 2025 figure. Rio Tinto has put its titanium business under strategic review.

Gakara: AFP reports a presidential order suspending foreign miners from 14 Jul 2021, which was not fetched. Rainbow still describes government actions as not in line with the mining convention, with no resolution as of Mar 2026. Historical offtake was not researched.

Mrima Hill: sources disagree on the Cortec licence date. afaa.ngo gives 2013; Citizen/bilaterals report a 10 Apr 2015 cancellation of 65 licences by CS Najib Balala. Resource figures in news (5.8 Mt Nb / 48.7 Mt REE, or 6.4/53.6 Mt) are unverified and not used. The tender winner and the outcome of the 9 Oct 2026 ruling are unknown.

Mrima Hill bidders: RareX and Iluka (AU) filed a joint application with NAMICO in Apr 2025. A US consortium, Mrima Earth Ltd, has also bid, and Chinese state companies reportedly signalled interest (https://miningmx.com/news/battery-minerals/2026-04-07-kenya-opens-bidding-for-prized-rare-earths-deposit). President Ruto said Kenya and the US finalised a preliminary agreement on the site (https://citizen.digital/article/petition-filed-to-stop-proposed-kenya-us-mrima-hill-mining-deal-n385178).

Mabounié: GabonReview (Feb 2026) says 'Eramet-Comilog en détient 76%', which contradicts Eramet's Nov 2022 sale of all assets to the state. Unresolved, not used. NEM/Dusk's stake, the state's share and the resource reporting code are unknown. Also involved: Indonesia (Perminas/Danantara) and Gulf (NEM, Abu Dhabi); Eramet (FR) exited in 2022.
No Japanese or Russian involvement was found in any of these projects.

Nigeria: none of the fetched sources say whether the monazite is a by-product of tin and columbite mining or tailings on the Jos Plateau, or which states produce it. USGS names no area or company. RMRDC sampled monazite in Kano, Taraba, Plateau, Kaduna and Bauchi in 2025.

Nigeria buyers: USGS MCS 2025 estimated Nigerian output from Chinese import data, which points to China as the buyer, but no fetched source gives monazite export tonnage by destination. The USGS 2024 chapter records tin, beryllium and tantalum going to China, but no destination for monazite.

Nigeria export ban: no gazetted ban on raw-mineral exports found. The Oct 2023 'era of exporting raw materials is over' line from the minister is a policy statement, and the USGS 2024 chapter mentions no restriction. Value addition seems to be enforced through licence conditions (search only).

Hasetins: is this an REE separation plant at all? Feedstock, flowsheet, products and the existing 6,000 t operation are all undisclosed. Rare Earth Exchanges (Dec 2025) says no Chinese ownership or partnership has been disclosed. Keep it, flag it, or drop it at merge.
Mineral sands rule: Kenmare sells monazite only inside a mixed concentrate (ZrTi). The same yes/no rule should apply across clusters, e.g. Madagascar or South African sands with incidental monazite.

Egypt Burullus: EBSC's head was quoted (Oct 2022) as expecting '145k tons of monazite' a year. That is implausible next to 298k t ilmenite and USGS world totals, and is probably a misquote. Treat it as unverified.
Kaduna polymetallic discovery with rare earths announced Jul 2026 at an Abuja summit (search snippet only; not fetched).

The USGS Tanzania reserve (890,000 t REO) almost matches Ngualla's JORC ore reserve of 887 kt REO in Peak's August 2025 scheme booklet. USGS likely took its figure from it, but USGS does not say so. Where USGS's South Africa figure (860,000 t) comes from is not stated.

In MCS 2026, Nigeria's 1,500 t no longer carries the 'estimated from Chinese import data' footnote. USGS says only that the revision is 'based on Government and industry reports'. Which reports, and why the figure dropped from 13,000 t to 1,500 t, is unexplained.

Burundi (Gakara), Angola and Malawi have no USGS rows. Any output is inside 'Other' (550 t in 2025), with no breakdown. The AU strategy says rare earths are 'mined' in Angola and South Africa, but USGS shows no output for either.
The AU strategy cites Madagascar at 960 t in 2023 (from USGS 2024). USGS 2025 gives 2,100 t for 2023. Madagascar's figures have moved a lot between editions.

Of the DFC's $62.8m, the $12.8m split among Malawi, Angola and Madagascar was not in the fetched Reuters text. Search snippets claiming $3.4m for Longonjo, a $4.6m grant for Songwe Hill and a potential EXIM loan of up to $160m for Pensana are unverified.
The AFC/Absa Longonjo loan was approved in March 2025, subject to conditions. No financial close was confirmed. A reported US$100m strategic investment in Pensana (December 2025) was not fetched.
Namibia: no gazette notice or legal instrument was found for the 2023 ban. It is not checked whether it was later amended, how it treats concentrates (such as Lofdal's), or whether it is enforced.
Malawi: the official text of the executive order was not found. Whether a mineral concentrate counts as 'processed' rests on Lindian's own statement; no government ruling was found.

Uganda: a January 2025 government post 'President Museveni Restates the Prohibition on The Export of Raw Minerals' (infrastructure.go.ug) returned 404. How the ban applies to Makuutu's mixed carbonate is unknown.

Zimbabwe: the December 2022 ban, a circular under the Base Minerals Export Control Act, covers lithium only (miningindex.co.zw). The 'SI 213/2022' designation appears only in search snippets. A reported later extension to all unrefined minerals (Mondaq) was not fetched. It is left out of export_rules because rare earths are not covered.
Ghana: the 2023 Green Minerals Policy and the December 2023 raw-lithium stance do not name rare earths in any source found. It is left out of export_rules.
EU: a second list of projects outside the EU has not been published. The 9 October 2026 list covered EU applications only, and the next call is due 'towards the end of 2026'.
JOGMEC/Lofdal: a Crux Investor report says JOGMEC and Toyota Tsusho completed their earn-in in July 2026. This is unverified; no company filing was fetched.

Not found: any US Minerals Security Partnership project list naming African rare-earth projects, any US-Malawi or US-Uganda critical-minerals MoU, or official confirmation of the February 2026 Rubio ministerial with African states.
